revisions.question: When a workable group decision is ready, I’m more comfortable delaying it to hear from the people most affected than moving ahead and gathering their feedback afterward.
revisions.desirability_balance: Both hearing people before the decision and moving ahead with later feedback are considerate, workable choices; the distinction is Yellow preference for voice and inclusion before closure.

revisions.question: A time-sensitive problem appears and no one clearly owns it. What contribution comes most naturally to you first?

options.label: Set a workable first direction and coordinate the next action
Generate a few fast possibilities and rally people around the most promising one
Check the immediate effects on people and coordinate the support they will need
Verify the critical facts and define a reliable first response

revisions.desirability_balance: Every option makes a useful contribution under time pressure; preference separates direction, possibility-generation, people support, and factual reliability.

revisions.question: Friends are choosing an activity, and the conversation has stalled. What contribution comes most naturally to you?

options.label: Narrow the workable choices and recommend one so the group can get going
Offer a fresh possibility that could bring some energy back to the group
Look for the choice that best fits the group’s shared mood and preferences
Compare time, cost, and logistics and suggest the most practical fit

revisions.desirability_balance: All four options help the group reasonably; Yellow expresses relational fit and harmony without implying that the other options exclude or disregard anyone.
